title: Cost-Driven Synthesis of Sound Abstract Interpreters

mechanism.domainTask: Sound abstract-transformer synthesis for neural-network verification
mechanism.populationDetail: One lowest-cost unsound transformer is retained between rounds; each round's candidate batch is temporary.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The one retained best code is the search incumbent, not a separate elite archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Batch completions are compared before updating the single incumbent, and a sound completion terminates search immediately.
mechanism.generationDetail: Initial DSL candidate is de novo; subsequent complete-code generation uses prior failed code as context, while a separate repair agent locally fixes invalid code.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: SMT soundness counterexamples and cost accompany AST/type diagnostics; the cost is the objective, not extra metadata.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The selected incumbent is generation context rather than an explicitly editable parent; repair acts on one invalid candidate.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: SMT counterexample-guided synthesis with a single cost-filtered incumbent and conditional code-repair agent.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Cost-Driven Synthesis of Sound Abstract Interpreters.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Generation is not clearly parent-editing despite incumbent context; L1/L2 may or may not share a backbone. Existing parent-selection citation should describe feedback reference selection, not a separate counterexample retrieval policy. Practical retry limit can return unsound fallback.
